subject: Retail Rivals: High latency + 502s after peering change (possible SNI mismatch)
messages:
From: Harper Lee <harper@retailrivals.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@retailrivals.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors: spike in 502/latency after peering move

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 502s and 500s for inference requests to our app at ~08:50 PDT after your team switched peering for our account (per the ticket notes). Latency for the affected endpoints climbed from 90ms p95 to ~1.2s and error rate spiked to ~7% for a 30m window.

Attached are a few sample error lines and a tcpdump from one of our edge hosts showing repeated TLS handshake retries when requests fail. We also noticed bursts of SYN/FIN in the captures.

This is impacting checkout flows. Can your network team look urgently? If you need a short call we can join now.

Thanks,
Harper
Harper Lee
SRE Lead, Retail Rivals
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Lee <harper@retailrivals.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: spike in 502/latency after peering move

Harper — thanks for the heads up and the captures. I'm escalating to our network team and looping in Jonas and Ben. We're treating this as Sev2 given checkout impact.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Jonas will validate peering/BGP tables and SNI handling at the edge.
- Ben will check the firewall/proxy ACLs and any recent rule push.
- I'll open a temporary traffic-shift to the prior peering region if we confirm the new path is unstable.

Can you confirm the exact edge hostname you captured (edge-12b.retailrivals.com?) and whether you saw any client-initiated TLS renegotiation?

I'll update you in 20 minutes.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harper Lee <harper@retailrivals.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: spike in 502/latency after peering move

Quick summary of what I see from initial triage:
- BGP/peering: The new peering fabric for Retail Rivals was advertised at 08:47 PDT and route propagation completed in ~2m. No immediate route flaps afterward.
- TLS handshake anomalies: The tcpdump shows multiple TLS ClientHello packets with SNI `api.retailrivals.com` but the next-hop balancer is responding with TCP RSTs on a subset of flows. On other flows the TLS handshake proceeds but then the backend closes the connection with 502.
- NAT/Proxy behavior: Our egress proxy (egress-proxy-3) was recently updated with stricter SNI-based routing rules as part of the peering cutover; I suspect an SNI match failure where proxy selects an incompatible egress cluster, leading to backend TLS mismatches and immediate resets.
- MTU: I verified MTU sizes between our edge and Retail Rivals' ASN — they match at 1500, not an immediate suspect.

Immediate mitigation I'm proposing (low-risk, reversible):
1) Temporarily disable SNI-only routing on egress-proxy-3 for traffic tagged to Retail Rivals (5 min change window).
2) Add an explicit fallback cluster that preserves original egress path to the pre-cutover peering for Retail Rivals.
3) If the above reduces errors, schedule a careful rollback of the new SNI rule and run a canary with 10% traffic for 30m.

I'll push the change and monitor. Attaching quick packet excerpt and our routing snapshot.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harper Lee <harper@retailrivals.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: spike in 502/latency after peering move

Change log: I applied mitigation step (1) — disabled SNI-only routing on egress-proxy-3 for Retail Rivals tag and enabled fallback cluster to pre-cutover peering (change id CHG-55671). Monitor cutoff at 09:54 PDT.

Observations so far (09:58): error rate dropped from 7% -> 0.8% in the affected endpoints and p95 latency fell back to ~110ms. No 502 spikes visible in the last 3m window.

I'll keep proxy in this relaxed mode while we validate. If stable after 30m we'll plan a controlled canary for the new SNI rules with explicit host-header checks and a circuit-breaker if 5xx > 1%.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Harper Lee <harper@retailrivals.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@retailrivals.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: spike in 502/latency after peering move

Tessa / team — thanks for the quick response. We saw immediate improvement after the proxy change and have no further customer-facing incidents during our peak window.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you produce an RCA that explains why the SNI rule selected an incompatible egress cluster? We need assurance before we re-enable the tighter routing.
- We expect an uptime credit for the checkout impact window (08:50–09:22 PDT). Please advise next steps for billing/credits.

Happy to join a post-mortem next week. Appreciate the fast mitigation.

—Harper
Harper Lee
SRE Lead, Retail Rivals
